title: Inference Integrator Kits and Sample Contracts
author: Maya Hernandez
body:
Overview

This page describes the "Inference Integrator Kits" — a bundled set of product artifacts, reference code, and legal/contract language intended to accelerate commercial pilots and early enterprise integrations across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. The kit focuses on three goals: reduce time-to-first-call, standardize SLO/billing expectations, and provide safe defaults for fidelity & cost controls.

Scope

- Audience: Solutions engineers, commercial onboarding teams, and platform integrators.
- Supported surfaces: API quickstart, SDK samples (Python/Go/Node), per-route SLO templates, instrumentation checklist, and two contract templates (pilot MSA + commercial addendum).
- Exclusions: This kit does not replace customer-specific security questionnaires or bespoke legal negotiations.

Contents of the Integrator Kit

1) Developer Quickstart (artifact)
- A one-page README with the minimum steps to make a successful inference call against a sandbox tenant.
- Includes: configuration example, API key provisioning steps, and test prompt sets that validate latency and token accounting.

2) SDK Reference Snippets
- Python: minimal streaming example, structured output parsing, and graceful retry logic.
- Node: serverless handler pattern with cold-start warmers.
- Go: typed response parsing and batch request example.

3) Per-route SLO and Billing Templates
- SLO profiles: Realtime (p50<120ms), Interactive (p50<250ms, p95<500ms), Batch (throughput targets).
- Billing mapping: per-route fidelity tag -> billing SKU guidance (see Pricing & Bundles section).

4) Observability & Instrumentation Checklist
- Required metrics: request_id, route, model_variant, latency_ms, tokens_generated, error_type.
- Recommended traces: end-to-end trace including API gateway, routing decision, and model backend.

5) Contract language snippets
- Pilot MSA: 30–90 day evaluation language, data handling, IP keep-out, and limited SLA exposure.
- Commercial addendum: model variant guarantees, rollback/fallback behavior, and burst capacity credits.

6) Playbook: pilot -> pilot-extension -> conversion steps

Bundles & Pricing Guidance

- Starter Bundle (pilot): 100k generation tokens, 30-day sandbox, 1 dedicated test tenant, basic observability retention (7 days).
- Conversion Bundle (production): configurable credits + reserved capacity options; suggested default: 1M tokens + 1 dedicated route slot + 30-day warm standby.

Pricing mapping (example table)
| Bundle | Included | Suggested billable SKU | Notes |
| Starter | 100k gen tokens, 30d retention | starter-pilot-credits | Non-billable during pilot until conversion 
| Conversion | 1M gen tokens, 30d retention, SLA 99.9% | route-reserve-small | Applies to single critical route; add-on for burst credits |

Recommendation: During pilots, use per-route fidelity flags to avoid charging high-cost variants for exploratory traffic (e.g., use smaller/quantized variants for telemetry-only flows).

Rollout and Adoption Playbook (Steps)

1. Pre-sales alignment (owner: solutions-engineering)
   - Share integrator kit and run a 60-minute technical onboarding demo.
   - Agree success criteria: latency targets, QA prompts, and business KPIs.
2. Sandbox provisioning (owner: platform-ops)
   - Create tenant, generate API key, and enable telemetry hooks.
3. Run initial telemetry tests (owner: customer + SE)
   - Execute the provided prompt-set (10–20 prompts covering edge-cases).
   - Validate metrics: p50, p95 latencies; token accounting; error rates <0.5%.
4. Pilot controls and guardrails (owner: customer + Redwood PM)
   - Apply per-route fidelity controls, set automatic fallback policies, and configure cost-alert thresholds.
5. Pilot review & conversion decision (owner: commercial lead)
   - Use the conversion checklist (performance, cost projections, compliance sign-offs).

Operational and SLAs (Suggested Defaults)

- Pilot-stage SLA: Informal, best-effort support; priority handling for SE escalations.
- Production-stage SLA: 99.9% uptime for route-reserve SKUs, p95 latency targets derived from selected SLO profile.
- Error budget handling: define monthly error budget and automatic fallback to compatible model variants when approaching error budget threshold.

Ownership and Contacts

- Kit Owner: Product Partnerships (primary contact: Maya Hernandez)
- Implementation support: Solutions Engineering (rotation list included in appendix).
- Legal & Contracts: Commercial Legal (contact: Diego Morales).

Appendix A — Example SDK snippet (Python)

```python
import redwood_sdk
client = redwood_sdk.Client(api_key="${API_KEY}")
resp = client.generate(route="customer-chat", prompt="Hello, summarize this ticket:")
print(resp.text)
```

Appendix B — Pilot MSA excerpt (contract language)

- Term: 60 days from execution.
- Data Handling: Customer data is isolated to the tenant, logs retained per the chosen retention policy.
- Liability cap: pilot-phase liability capped to fees paid during pilot.

Appendix C — Minimal telemetry checklist (table)
| Metric | Threshold (example) | Owner | Action if breached |
| latency_p95 | <500ms | Customer + SE | Auto-fallback to quantized model |
| error_rate | <0.5% | SE | Open high-priority ticket |
| tokens_generated | N/A | Finance | Review monthly usage |

Frequently Asked Questions (short)

Q: Can a pilot incur charges?
A: Pilots are typically non-billable until conversion; if customers use high-cost variants during pilot without explicit agreement, we reserve the right to bill or require conversion.

Q: Who signs the addendum for production credits?
A: The commercial lead together with Legal executes the addendum; typical signers: VP Engineering (customer) + Redwood Commercial Director.
